title: Sandbagging heuristic playbook
content:
Purpose and quick note:

This is a personal scratchpad for the "sandbagging" approach — intentionally injecting controlled difficulty and constraints into prompt libraries to stress-test model stability and reveal brittle failure modes. The goal is pragmatic: generate a compact set of heuristics and templates we can drop into the prompt-lab harness (DE-412) and quickly evaluate across multiple open models and quantization variants.

Why 'sandbagging'?
- Not adversarial red-team in the sense of trying to break safety; instead, we create mild-to-medium friction (ambiguity, token budgets, context truncation, conflicting instructions) to surface where output quality collapses.
- Helps identify non-obvious regressions when switching model variants or enabling batching/kv-cache optimizations.

Guiding principles (rough):
- Start small: one perturbation variable per run (e.g., drop 1 exemplar, shorten context by 30%).
- Keep examples labeled and canonical so diffs are traceable.
- Capture both objective markers (BLEU/EM/F1 where applicable) and subjective signals (clarity, hallucination, instruction-following).

Heuristic catalog (short defs):
1) Instruction Dilution: Append an extra high-level instruction that conflicts weakly with the main directive (e.g., "Also, be brief"). Tests whether model re-prioritizes.
2) Example Scrambling: Shuffle few-shot order or swap a positive example with a partially wrong one. Checks sample-sensitivity.
3) Budget Trimming: Reduce token allowance for expected answer (simulate truncation/low-cost mode).
4) Context Noise: Inject irrelevant paragraphs (safe but off-topic) between system instruction and shots.
5) Alias/Name Swap: Replace entity names with anonymized tokens to probe referential robustness.
6) Ambiguous Constraint: Introduce a vague requirement ("make it professional, but casual") to reveal style inconsistency.
7) Syntactic Perturbation: Break punctuation or formatting — tests tokenization fragile spots.
8) Fallback Sim: Remove model-specific special tokens or tool hints (e.g., function signatures).

Core templates (placeholders: {{INSTR}}, {{SHOTS}}, {{CONTEXT}}, {{BUDGET}})
- Base: "You are an assistant. {{INSTR}} Provide the answer concisely."
- Sandbag-1 (dilution): "You are an assistant. {{INSTR}} Also, keep it under 40 tokens and minimize explanation. Provide the answer concisely."
- Sandbag-2 (noise): "You are an assistant. {{CONTEXT}}
IGNORE the paragraph above when answering. {{SHOTS}}
{{INSTR}}"
- Sandbag-3 (scramble): "You are an assistant. Here are examples (note: order random): {{SHOTS_SCRAMBLED}}
{{INSTR}}"

Example few-shot set (for QA -> conversion):
- Shot A:
  Q: Convert this to a bullet list: "Top 3 benefits of X"
  A: - Benefit one
     - Benefit two
     - Benefit three
- Shot B (partial-wrong):
  Q: Convert this to a bullet list: "Key things about Y"
  A: - First thing (note: includes an extra commentary that is not strictly bullet)
- Test prompt (Base):
  INSTR: "Convert the following short paragraph into 3 bullets. Keep each bullet <= 12 words."
  CONTEXT: "Short paragraph: Several teams benefited from lower latency, predictable costs, and better observability."

Planned sandbag variations for the test grid:
- baseline (no perturbation)
- dilution (append 'also be brief')
- budget_trim (budget=30 tokens)
- noise_insert (add 2 unrelated sentences before shots)
- scramble_shots (shuffle)
- partial_corrupt (replace one shot answer with a subtly incorrect version)

Expected failure signals to log (auto and manual):
- Auto: answer length > budget, missing required list format, token-level diffs high, generation truncated marker, non-empty hallucination_count (via heuristics).
- Manual: answers that add speculative facts, inconsistent style across bullets, ignores instruction to limit words.

Quick experiment harness notes (for DE-412):
- Run across model variants: redwood-mini-13b-fp16, open-ggml-7b-q4, rwd-xl-quant:1 (names approximate).
- For each run capture: prompt hash, variant label, quant flag, batching on/off, avg latency, tokens_in/tokens_out, success flags (meets format/length).
- Add a flag for 'simulate-context-loss' that drops last 20% of context before inference.

Failure case snippets we've already seen in ad-hoc runs:
- Under budget_trim the model often still writes full sentences instead of bullets -> likely decoding temp/penalty config ignoring length instruction.
- Example Scramble flips which exemplar the model parrots — sometimes it uses the second shot's style entirely.
- Noise insert occasionally makes the model repeat the noise as part of the answer when the instruction to ignore isn't high-salience.

Practical mitigations to try (order of preference):
- Explicit formatting guards: include a start/end token around desired answer block and request JSON output when possible.
- Strong negative examples: include a short exemplar that demonstrates the forbidden behavior (e.g., a 'wrong' example that shows long-paragraph output with label 'bad').
- Token budget enforcement: enforce truncation at runtime (post-process) and mark as 'failed' if important markers missing.
- Instruction anchoring: put the hard constraint at the top of the system message and repeat in the last line before shots.

Open questions & next steps (todo):
- Which perf knobs in the runtime cause 'length instruction' ignoring? (Compile kernels? decoding settings?) Assign to @Evan for instrumentation.
- How to present sandbagged runs in console UX? propose a small chevron toggler 'show perturbations' on per-eval card. (product task)
- Need a small canonical dataset of ~40 prompts for cross-model regression; build a seed from existing eval buckets + 10 new sandbag cases.
- Try overlaying quantization profiles (q4 vs q5) to see pattern.

Ad-hoc notes (messy):
- When testing with streaming ON, the model often starts streaming the noise chunk as part of first event -> consider sending a short priming token or wait for EOS to be stable.
- Thought: Could add a 'grace exemplar' that shows minimal output but encodes the format strongly (eg: {"answer":["one","two"]}) to push JSON-form. Might reduce hallucination.

Small checklist for the next dev pass:
- [ ] finalize 40-item sandbag prompt set
- [ ] wire tests into DE-412 harness and add failure metrics
- [ ] run grid for 3 models x 4 quant flavors x with/without batching
- [ ] collate top-10 failure archetypes and capture representative traces

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally informal. Drop in experiments, rough examples, and trash until we've distilled a shipping playbook. If something looks stable, migrate to shared_drives/engineering/developer-experience/playbooks/sandbagging-v1.md

-- Samira

Snippets (copyable templates):
Base prompt (with placeholders):
"SYSTEM: You are a concise assistant.
{{CONTEXT}}
EXAMPLES:
{{SHOTS}}
TASK: {{INSTR}}
OUTPUT: Provide a JSON array of bullets, maximum {{BUDGET}} tokens total."

Dilution variant quick paste:
"SYSTEM: You are a concise assistant. Also keep responses short and avoid extra commentary.
...rest..."

End of scratchpad.
